summary: South Korean Interim Government Activities No. 24 covers September 1947 and is the first monthly report for which the South Korean Interim Government, rather than SCAP's Statistics and Research Section, takes full responsibility. Its six parts report population movements, vested property, food collection, prices, agriculture, mining, industry, trade, labor, transport, communications, finance, politics and social affairs. The month was dominated by the death of Military Governor Major General Archer L. Lerch on 11 September, Brigadier General C. G. Helmick becoming Acting Military Governor, the second anniversary of USAMGIK, the franchise law (Public Law No. 5) for popular election of the Legislative Assembly, and press reaction to the American four-power conference proposal and the Soviet withdrawal proposal. Historians will find detailed tables on rice collection quotas, coal output, the 18 billion won budget, bank note issue, refugee inflow from the North and school enrollment, plus frank statements of the limits of Korean statistical reporting.
highlights: Military Governor Major General Archer L. Lerch died at 0758 on 11 September; Brigadier General C. G. Helmick, Acting Military Governor since 7 September, announced it, and funeral services were held before the National Capitol in Seoul on 16 September.

On 3 September Helmick signed Public Law No. 5, the franchise law for popular election of Korean Interim Legislative Assembly members; no election was to be held until at least 80 days after a 15-member Central Election Committee is chosen.

Moderate leaders including Civil Administrator Ahn Chai Hong and KILA Speaker Kimm Kiu Siu announced the Minju Dok Dang (Democratic Independence Party) on 23 September, with Hong Myung Hi as temporary chairman.
The 1947 rice collection program from 1 November sets the farmer price at 640 won per 54-kg bag; summer grain collection reached 88.3 percent of its 711,000 suk quota by 25 September.

Population movement from October 1945 to 22 September 1947 shows 885,532 outbound, mostly Japanese, against 2,332,458 inbound, including 1,110,513 Koreans from Japan and 838,263 Koreans from north of the 38th parallel.

The SKIG 1947-48 budget stood at about 18 billion won on 30 September after supplementals, up from the 17,720,227,310 won approved on 2 July; Bank of Chosun note issue rose 1.8 billion won from July to September.

Labor Department Orders No. 1 and 2 of 15 September implemented the Child Labor Law, and the Seoul Electric Company reinstatement dispute over three discharged workers drew pressure from the Northwestern Youth Association.

Education statistics report 3,058,433 students enrolled in South Korean schools at 31 July 1947, including 13,827 in 25 universities and colleges; the fall typhoid immunization program began 15 September.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover, title page and table of contents for Number 24, September 1947, listing six parts from Basic Aspects to Social.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: States that No. 24 is the first report for which the South Korean Interim Government has full responsibility; warns that statistics are incomplete and charts await SCAP drawings.

sections.title: Part I: Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Population movement since 1945, with net inflow near 1.5 million, and Office of Property Custody income, leases, staff and policy on vested Japanese property.

sections.title: Section 1. Population
sections.summary: Net inflow of about 1.45 million people; 20,394 illegal Korean entrants returned from Japan; refugee flow from the North rising; Office of Foreign Affairs handled Chinese junks and Japanese repatriation costs.

sections.title: Repatriation
sections.summary: Since October 1945, 885,532 people left and 2,332,458 arrived; the ship Kogane Maru carried 797 Koreans from Japan on 12 September.

sections.title: Refugees
sections.summary: Refugee arrivals from north of the 38th parallel exceeded 1946 levels from May to August 1947, with Pyongan-pukto the leading origin.

sections.title: Activities
sections.summary: Chinese junk permits at Inchon, Japanese repatriation cost of $177,199.56 in CARIOA supplies, Korean registration in Japan, and 13 Korean students cleared for study in the US.

sections.title: Section 2. Vested Property
sections.summary: Property Custody income shifted from rents to sales and confiscations; Korean staff rose to 2,062 by 30 September; Helmick ruling and 1 September bonding memorandum for managers.

sections.title: Income
sections.summary: Rents fell from over 75 percent of income before 1947 to 27 percent in the first half of 1947 as sales and confiscations grew.

sections.title: Properties Under Lease
sections.summary: Vested residences under lease rose from 51,256 at 31 December 1946 to 57,505 at 30 June 1947, Seoul City alone reaching 11,494; no income breakdown between residential and non-residential leases exists.

sections.title: Employment
sections.summary: Korean employees of the Office of Property Custody grew from 895 in December 1946 to 2,062 (budgeted) in September 1947.

sections.title: Activities
sections.summary: Rising Sun Petroleum frozen-asset inquiry for the British Consul General, Helmick's ruling on companies occupying Army-needed buildings, and a bonding memorandum for managers.

sections.title: Part II: Production and Supply
sections.summary: Summer grain and rice collection, prices, agriculture, coal and metals, industrial output, foreign trade and labor in South Korea, August-September 1947.

sections.title: Section 1. Food Supply
sections.summary: Summer grain collection reached 88.3 percent of the 711,000 suk quota by 25 September; 1947 rice collection set at 640 won per 54-kg bag with provincial quotas assigned.

sections.title: Indigenous Foods
sections.summary: Cumulative summer grain collection from July to 25 September 1947 against a 711,000 suk polished-grain quota.

sections.title: Rice Collection, 1946 Crop
sections.summary: On 10 September 413,130 suk of 1946 rice remained on hand out of 3,560,866 suk purchased.

sections.title: Imports
sections.summary: September grain imports to South Korea were 33,574 metric tons, near the January-August monthly average; cumulative imports since May 1946 reached 520,256 tons, mostly wheat.

sections.title: Grain Released for Rations
sections.summary: Grain other than rice released for rations roughly equalled rice May-July 1947; in August it was 356,376 suk against 184,661 suk of rice, 65 percent of the total.

sections.title: Population on Rations
sections.summary: Population on general and special rations rose from 7,718,526 in March to 8,720,198 in August 1947; supplementary rations peaked at 395,697. Ration set at 2.2 hop (1,155 calories) daily.

sections.title: Rice Collection Program, 1947
sections.summary: Program beginning 1 November sets the farmer price at 640 won per bag and removes subsidies; provincial quotas are in polished rice.

sections.title: Section 2. Prices
sections.summary: National Economic Board Administrative Study No. 5 on the 'rice formula', Seoul price tables through July 1947, gold prices, and pricing of vested-factory goods.

sections.title: Administrative Study No. 5
sections.summary: Explains the October 1946 rice formula, polished rice at 55 times base prices, revocation of National Price Regulation No. 1 on 30 June, and 10 to 15 percent factory profit margins.

sections.title: Price Trends
sections.summary: Bank of Chosun Seoul tables show grain and bean prices still rising through July 1947 while other foods and textiles held steady.

sections.title: Gold
sections.summary: The August 1947 open-market wholesale gold price was a preliminary 2,425 won per don, over five times the 473 of August 1945 and more than three times the year before.

sections.title: Activities, National Price Administration
sections.summary: In September prices were set on over 20 lots of goods, from underwear to pharmaceuticals and tar paper, balancing inflation against manufacturer profit.

sections.title: Section 3. Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
sections.summary: 1947 rice estimate held at 14,200,000 suk (2,164,000 metric tons); winter hay goal of 1,500,000 tons, cotton on 125,000 hectares, rural youth clubs, forestry and fisheries.

sections.title: Bureau of Agricultural Economics
sections.summary: Statistics staff sent to the field for a final pre-harvest rice estimate; straw bag work.

sections.title: Livestock
sections.summary: Winter hay program to store 1,500,000 tons, hay selling at 12 won per kwan; livestock conditions across South Korea.

sections.title: Production
sections.summary: Potatoes from imported seed were harvested in Kangwon-do despite late planting and wild boar losses.

sections.title: Cotton and Fiber
sections.summary: Cotton sown on about 125,000 hectares, expected yield over 17 million kg of seed cotton against 10,651,434 kg in 1946; sericulture.

sections.title: Farm Supply
sections.summary: Cholla-namdo collected 4,000 suk of vetch seed for green manure; meeting held on compost and fertilizer distribution.

sections.title: Irrigation
sections.summary: Korean Irrigation Association let contracts to resume five tidal projects (estimated cost 57,473,253 won; bids 40,544,000 won), and on 20 September marked completion of the Son San, Ko Ah and Kim O San projects.

sections.title: Suwon Experiment Station
sections.summary: Suwon station drew up a new table of organization placing the Central Station at bureau level, and a Japanese study of fertilizers and rice root development was translated and mimeographed.

sections.title: Korea Agricultural Association
sections.summary: KAA ran a farmer lecture course for 50 men in Kyonggi-do and filed its fiscal-year report; fertilizer sales reached 119,347 metric tons, 85 percent of receipts, with 457,685,968 won collected.

sections.title: Rural Youth Activities
sections.summary: Rural youth clubs specialize in gardening, livestock, sericulture and forestry; some elect girls as officers.

sections.title: Forestry
sections.summary: Provincial Forestry Advisers met in Seoul 7-9 October; rough Army lumber was exchanged for dressed lumber on 2 September; Inchon plywood plant cleared to produce about 20,000 sheets monthly.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: Fisheries data were limited; the motor mine sweeper YNS 200 was released for deep-sea fishing, and Seoul Public Market received 68.65 tons of fish and marine products in the week ending 20 September.

sections.title: Section 4. Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: Anthracite and lignite output fell in August; bituminous coal demand and Coal Committee proceedings; gold, silver, copper and tungsten, with tungsten hit by the 3 August flood.

sections.title: Coal
sections.summary: Anthracite peaked in June and lignite in July before dropping in August; Samchuk, Eunsung and Hwasun mines, bituminous coal and the Coal Committee.

sections.title: Metals
sections.summary: Gold, silver, copper, electrolytic copper and tungsten output; tungsten production fell after the August flood.

sections.title: Section 5. Industrial Production and Allocations
sections.summary: Flour output fell to 236 metric tons, the lowest on record; textiles, paper, nails, briquettes, rubber, tobacco and salt, plus allocations of metal and controlled commodities.

sections.title: Processed Foods
sections.summary: One of two government flour mills closed for lack of wheat; Tong-A Food Products canned peaches and made soy sauce.

sections.title: Textiles
sections.summary: 1,589 bales of raw cotton arrived in early August (1,200 UNRRA), keeping vested mills running at reduced output; two of seven mills made 46-52 percent of July-August yarn.

sections.title: Paper
sections.summary: August paper output was 312.8 metric tons, below July's 362.3, from one mill breakdown and coal shortage though 10 of 14 vested mills increased; first Japanese cylinder-face parts arrived.

sections.title: Machinery and Hardware
sections.summary: August nail output in two vested plants was 140.9 metric tons, nearly 20 percent below July, from sulphuric acid and wire shortages; Inchon Nail Company furnaces were repaired and another added in September.

sections.title: Other Industries
sections.summary: Briquette output fell almost 50 percent in two months to 11,000 tons in August; Chosun Onada Cement reopened 1 August making 6,147 tons; brick, firebrick, and rubber shoe output declined.

sections.title: Monopoly Bureau Products
sections.summary: Tobacco output declined in August; salt production rose but stayed low because rains lasted until mid-August.

sections.title: Allocations
sections.summary: Metal allocated to manufacturers 18 August to 13 September, controlled commodities, and 80 tons of aluminum scrap at Kimpo Air Base.

sections.title: Agencies of Distribution
sections.summary: The Federation of Financial Associations and Federation of Distributing Associations distribute domestic controlled goods; FFA purchases fell from 164,266 thousand won in July to 37,627 thousand in September.

sections.title: Section 6. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: July private-trade imports fell 86.6 percent from June and exports fell 21 percent; trade with the US, Japan, Hong Kong and Egypt; civilian supply imports of salt and fertilizer.

sections.title: Private Trade
sections.summary: Largest July exports were 965 tons of metals worth 64 million won; imports included salt, cornstarch and 4,906 bottles of penicillin.

sections.title: Trade with United States, Japan, Hong Kong and Egypt
sections.summary: USCC will cancel its Korea export contract at 31 December 1947; direct Hong Kong trade resumed; Egypt barter of 3,000 cotton bales for 700 tons scheelite; PX souvenir sales reached 3,406 dollars.

sections.title: Imports, Services of Civilian Supply
sections.summary: Civilian supply imports of salt (908 tons total in August), fertilizer, foodstuffs and other goods, with transportation.

sections.title: Section 7. Labor
sections.summary: Child labor orders of 15 September, Seoul Electric Company reinstatement dispute, Korean Industrial Health Association, and unemployment sampling in Seoul, Kyonggi-do and Chungchong-pukto.

sections.title: Labor Regulations
sections.summary: Labor Department Orders No. 1 and 2 of 15 September implement the Child Labor Law and require education for child workers under eighteen.

sections.title: Labor Union Activities
sections.summary: Seoul Electric Company shop stewards and the dispute over three discharged workers, pressed by the Northwestern Youth Association.

sections.title: Labor Education
sections.summary: Translation of 'Duties of a Shop Steward' and radio talks on the Child Labor Law and collective bargaining.

sections.title: Labor Conference
sections.summary: Provincial labor bureau chiefs met for three days from 25 August 1947; they backed the Child Labor Law, thought Maximum Working Hours too strict, and were told to staff a new Industrial Health and Welfare section.

sections.title: Industrial Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Korean Industrial Health Association formed 19 August by 14 industrial physicians, who began drafting a charter.

sections.title: Unemployment
sections.summary: Samples from 1947 registration show 20-30 percent of persons over 15 unemployed, and employment near 40 to 43 percent.

sections.title: Part III: Public Services
sections.summary: Railroad finances and marine fuel costs, communications revenue and air mail start, electric power, public works man-days, and housing for dispossessed Koreans and refugees.

sections.title: Section 1. Transportation
sections.summary: August railroad outlay exceeded income for the first time in fiscal 1947-48; rising bunker fuel prices may force a 40 percent marine freight rate increase.

sections.title: Field of Transportation
sections.summary: Railroads accounted for 99 percent of Department of Transportation income and 92 percent of expenditures in August.

sections.title: Railroads
sections.summary: Passenger revenue over 90 percent of income but passengers declining since May; freight tonnage and rates, equipment, employment and coal consumption.

sections.title: Marine Transport
sections.summary: Diesel oil rose from 8 to 16 won per gallon and bituminous coal from 650 to 1,200 won per ton; Ports and Harbors Committee report.

sections.title: Highway Transport and Selected Activities
sections.summary: About 5,000 Army-condemned tires went to the Korean Automobile Supply Company; 50,774 railroad ties arrived from the United States (212,000 in six weeks), and a Taejon creosoting plant started.

sections.title: Section 2. Communications
sections.summary: Revenue rose from 19.2 million won in June to 31.9 million in August; worldwide air mail began 1 October with a 50-won stamp; postal savings and bureau activities.

sections.title: Postal Savings and Insurance
sections.summary: Postal savings and insurance statistics from the Department of Communications.

sections.title: Activities
sections.summary: Postal, Communications, Fiscal and Supply Bureau work, including air mail to all parts of the world from 1 October and weekly mail volume to Japan and the United States.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Utilities
sections.summary: Electricity delivered reached 65 million KWH in July then fell 4 million in August; Bureau of Utilities work and streetcar operations.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Works
sections.summary: Public works man-days and wages peaked in May, dipped in June and rose in August; highways, city planning and the National Board of Fire Commissioners.

sections.title: Section 5. Housing
sections.summary: The 350 twenty-pyung houses for dispossessed Koreans were 85 percent complete on 30 September, delayed to 15 October by glass shortage; occupation set for 13 October.

sections.title: Part IV: Finance
sections.summary: Government budget of 18 billion won, note issue, receipts, taxation and civilian supply program, plus bank cash, deposits, loans and insurance.

sections.title: Section 1. Government Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosun note issue up 1.8 billion won July to September; 1947-48 budget at 18 billion won; 69 percent of 1946-47 taxes collected; civilian supply program and Controller of Commodities.

sections.title: Note Issue of the Bank of Chosun
sections.summary: Note issue grew 1.8 billion won, probably linked to SKIG overdraft borrowing.

sections.title: Budget of the South Korea Interim Government
sections.summary: Budget approved 2 July at 17,720,227,310 won reached 18 billion with supplementals; the National Economic Board reviewed supplementals on 30 September.

sections.title: Monthly Receipts and Payments
sections.summary: Monthly government receipts and payments tables.

sections.title: Taxation
sections.summary: 69 percent of 1946-47 assessments collected, 31 percent outstanding; a study found enforcement facilities wholly inadequate.

sections.title: Civilian Supply Program
sections.summary: Funds and goods of the civilian supply program.

sections.title: Office of Controller of Commodities
sections.summary: Functions of the Office of Controller of Commodities.

sections.title: Section 2. Non-Government Finance
sections.summary: Seven banks and 401 financial associations: cash balances, deposits, government-guaranteed industrial loans, life and damage insurance, and institution activities.

sections.title: Financial Institutions and Cash Balance
sections.summary: Seven banks including the Bank of Chosun and 401 associations tied to the Federation of Financial Associations.

sections.title: Deposits in Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Tables of deposits by type and institution.

sections.title: Loans by Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Loans to industry and commerce, with government-guaranteed loans reflecting SKIG interest in industrial development.

sections.title: Life and Damage Insurance
sections.summary: Life and damage insurance statistics.

sections.title: Activities of the Financial Institutions
sections.summary: Activities of banks and financial associations during the month.

sections.title: Part V: Government and Politics
sections.summary: Death of Military Governor Lerch and Helmick's succession, the franchise law, Ordinance No. 151, the new Minju Dok Dang, party statements and the National Safety Campaign.

sections.title: Section 1. Administration
sections.summary: Helmick became Acting Military Governor 7 September; Lerch died 11 September, with services on 16 September; Helmick's 12 September statement on USAMGIK's second anniversary.

sections.title: Section 2. Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Public Law No. 5 on popular election signed 3 September; Ordinance No. 151 on judges and prosecutors, 30 September; Japanese currency use, KILA sessions and roster.

sections.title: Section 3. Political Developments
sections.summary: Moderates formed the Minju Dok Dang on 23 September; General Albert E. Brown spoke at the Democratic Party of Korea's second anniversary; rightist, leftist and neutral party statements.

sections.title: Section 4. Internal Security
sections.summary: National Safety Campaign extended to 1 October after 127 accidents and 15 deaths in August; 100 police cadets began advanced training on 3 September.

sections.title: Part VI: Social
sections.summary: Public information broadcasts and film review, Korean press reaction to the four-power conference and Soviet withdrawal proposals, education enrollment, and public health.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Information
sections.summary: Department of Public Information reviewed 44 films (21 Korean, 17 American); 'Government Hour' radio programs covered the general election, plus a new opera series.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Opinion and the Press
sections.summary: Editorials on the American four-power conference proposal, UN presentation of the Korean problem, the Soviet withdrawal proposal and Lerch's death, plus tables of South Korean publications.

sections.title: Four-Power Conference Proposal
sections.summary: Han Sung Ilbo welcomed the American proposal, while extreme rightist papers attacked the Moscow Decision.

sections.title: Presentation of Korean Problem to the United Nations
sections.summary: Press comment on taking the Korean problem to the United Nations.

sections.title: Soviet Proposal for Withdrawal from Korea
sections.summary: Choong Ang Shin Mun called the Soviet withdrawal plan a diplomatic gesture; Dai Dong Sinmoon warned early withdrawal meant civil war.

sections.title: Political Activities, Death of Lerch, and Publications
sections.summary: Editorials of condolence on Lerch's death on 12 September and tables of publications by frequency and political character.

sections.title: Section 3. Education
sections.summary: 3,058,433 students enrolled at 31 July 1947, 13,827 in 25 universities; new School of Veterinary Medicine, American Language Institute, textbooks and Korean National Youth leadership training.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Typhoid immunization began 15 September after August vaccine output of 7,091,000 cc; quarantine regulations of 4 September; midwife licensing rule of 12 September; dental, sanitation, narcotics and veterinary work.
